limits: Covers the overall verdict /cpp:status reads (issue #1290): a home whose only enabled capability completes an MCP initialize + tools/list handshake reads `ready` (exit 0); a second-opinion endpoint with nothing listening, in the shipped `${SECOND_OPINION_URL:-http://127.0.0.1:<port>}/mcp` form, and an installed flow helper deleted from a current checkout's install, each read NOT ready. Cases are SITUATIONS built fresh by run-case.sh from a one-word scenario, because a closed port must be closed at run time and a nested repository cannot be committed. DECLARED GAPS: conflicting scopes, a stdio server that exits before initialize, an old checkout, a failed freshness lookup, credential redaction and the clean-home install/update smoke are pinned by tests/test_capability_readiness.py, not registered here; the healthy case leaves flow DISABLED (an empty home), so a flow row reading ready is proven by the tests and the missing-helper case proves only that a broken flow install is not ready. No case reaches a real second-opinion or playwright server - a live handshake against a host's servers is host evidence, not a committed case.

anchors.why: The pre-fix check lived in a markdown fence, not a script, so there is no file to vendor byte-for-byte. The anchor is lines 279-293 of status.md at 51dc14d reproduced VERBATIM between markers, plus a constructed preamble that takes the gate's argv and enters the project directory (sha `n/a` because the file as a whole is constructed; tests/test_capability_readiness.py compares the verbatim span against 51dc14d). It greps the first url out of .mcp.json - `http://127.0.0.1:<port>}/mcp`, brace included, from the shipped `${SECOND_OPINION_URL:-...}` form - curls it, prints `[~] not verified reachable` and exits 0 whatever it finds, and it never looks at flow at all. So it misses both bad cases: that is the #1290 defect itself, an installed-or-registered check standing in for a usable one.
